newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Prods Outlook--Tosco, Exxon FCCs feed bulls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Prods Outlook--Tosco, Exxon FCCs feed bulls.

text.p: Tosco Corp, tightly controlling the information flow surrounding the restart of its huge catalytic cracker in New Jersey, appeared poised to prolong bullishness in U.S. gasoline markets, traders said.
Exxon, with fluid cat cracker issues of its own in Houston, was causing uncertainty in the oil patch, where traders were trying to figure out just how long that unit would remain out of service.
NYMEX markets reflected talk Tosco was cranking up its cat after completing work on it, but cash markets were not ready to admit the bullish stampede was over this week.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Tosco kept gasoline markets in New York Harbor on edge Monday morning, with some predicting the current state of affairs could continue for much of this week as the company attempts to minimize the financial impact of three weeks of maintenance at its cat cracker at Bayway in New Jersey.

Tosco sources had said the 150,00 barrel-per-day unit, the largest in the world, would return to operation August 16, and the NYMEX market seemed to be reflecting that. But cash traders were more circumspect.
"The (cash) market is still very strong. It's in a 'wait-and-see' mode to see if Tosco comes out and does some selling," said one trader.

He added he expects Tosco, the biggest gasoline supplier in the Harbor, to make those buyers holding their breath for Bayway's return to rush to the table later this week gasping for breath to close pricey deals for "A2" regular reformulated gasoline.
Prompt A2 was heard done as high as 9.00 cents over September NYMEX on Friday, and was heard offered at 9.25 cents over in the early going on Monday.

"Why would someone with the power to move the market refrain from using it?" asked another trader, who said Tosco's coyness and apparent reluctance to sell so quickly struck him as a textbook example of how to make lemonade from lemons.

Underpining the bullish effects of the Bayway outage is solid demand, which traders saw remained very real notwithstanding the exaggerated backwardation on the NYMEX gasoline screen of nearly 6.00 cents a gallon.
"Some of the strength in the paper market may be questionable, but the strength in underlying demand is very real," the second trader said.
U.S. GULF

The shutdown of the 110,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker at Exxon's Baytown, Texas refinery last week drove differentials sharply higher as the company moved to cover commitments in the spot market.
However, estimates for a restart of the unit varied from a few days to three weeks, heightening market anxieties about the availability of gasoline over the short term.
U.S. Gulf traders indeed appeared reluctant to speculate on market direction for the coming week, though gasoline prices would likely continue their choppy movement.
"I don't know what to expect," one Gulf trader said. "We should see a lot of volatility," the trader added.

Conventional M1 gasoline prices in the Gulf sat at about 66.50 cents a gallon by late Friday, reflecting a gain of about 6.00 cents from earlier in the week. That gain came on the heal of a 5-cent selloff in the prompt barrels.
However, Gulf Coast heating oil and low sulphur diesel markets were seen sliding sideways this week, with ample supplies preventing any sharp price movements, according to market watchers.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent unleaded gasoline differentials were seen as staying largely steady this week after falling off Monday morning.
"We were high because most of the demand had been for barrels by the 15th," said a Group Three trader, adding strong values in the Harbor will keep Midcontinent markets from dropping further.
Supply was also seen as stabilizing in the region following tight inventories last week due to refinery glitches, including cut production at Ashland's Minnesota plant due to a minor leak.
"There is plenty of gasoline right now," said a Midco trader.
